newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine Stock Exchange plans index this year.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine Stock Exchange plans index this year.

text.p: The Ukrainian Stock Exchange plans to begin a stock index in the second half of this year, when it expects the government to sell 20-30 large enterprises, the exchange's vice-president said on Monday.

"We have suggested the government sell shares in 20-30 large enterprises, a move which would give us the ability to establish market prices for shares and increase Ukraine's budget revenues," Vladimir Odintsov told a news conference.
He added the State Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, supported the move but was awaiting government approval.

Odintsov said the lack of an index was limiting the exchange's development and inflow of foreign investment into Ukraine, which has received only about $1.4 billion in private foreign investment since independence in 1991.
Odintsov estimated sale of shares in the enterprises would double stock market activity. In 1996 turnover rose to 31.6 million hryvnias from 5.2 million hryvnias the previous year.
Bankers blame low activity on the exchange on the slow pace of privatisation, as few major enterprises have been sold off.
Business is also shared by several other exchanges including the Kiev International Stock Exchange, the Donetsk exchange in eastern Ukraine, and a Kiev-based OTC market. ($1 = $1.8785 hryvnia)
